title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  inaugurates RBI’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
subtitle:
A major step towards a more secure financial system; The RBI's new facilities in Bhubaneswar will strengthen digital infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities: PM

With the blessings of Mahaprabhu, today Bhubaneswar is giving a new institution to the new India; The inauguration of both the RBI's Data Centre and the Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar is a significant occasion; This will be very beneficial for the people of Odisha and the country: PM

We are driven by a model of Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance; To us, development means the equitable progress of India, where opportunities reach our villages and small towns alike: PM

Today, digital banking has connected every Indian to 24-hour banking services: PM

Today, even those who have nothing to offer as a guarantee to the bank are able to start their own work by availing affordable and accessible loans; From small entrepreneurs to traditional artisans, from street vendors to workers in the unorganized sector, for the first time, they have received the benefits of formal banking: PM

The past decade was about taking banking to those who were deprived of it; The coming decade is about making banking more efficient and more reliable: PM

Nowadays, wars are not fought with weapons alone; A nation can also be weakened by attacking its economy. And as India grows economically stronger, we must protect our banking system from cyber looters and cyber terrorists: PM
date:
Posted On:
                25 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Invoking the blessings of Mahaprabhu Jagannath, the Prime Minister celebrated Bhubaneswar gifting a vital new institution to New India. He congratulated the RBI and everyone involved in launching both facilities. “This will be very beneficial for the people of Odisha and the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the broader significance of the inauguration, the Prime Minister stated that the event demonstrates a fundamental shift in the nation's administrative approach. He emphasized that contemporary governance is anchored in prioritizing development, expanding its scale, and ensuring last-mile delivery. "Today’s program is proof of how the approach to Governance has changed in India,” noted PM Modi.
The Prime Minister detailed the shift toward a Pro-People, Pro-Active Good Governance model focused on balanced regional growth, dignity for the poor, and ensuring no citizen is left behind. He highlighted that expressways are now connecting small towns, institutions like AIIMS have expanded across numerous states, medical colleges are being opened in smaller towns, nearly 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been established in villages, and digital connectivity is expanding across remote areas. “Making the life of the citizen easier and giving new opportunities to their dreams is now the real purpose of Governance,” asserted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister pointed out that although banks were nationalized in the 1960s and 1970s in the name of the poor, over half the population remained outside the banking ecosystem until 2014, when bank loans were a distant dream for the middle class and unthinkable for small farmers, the landless, and women. He noted that the modern era of financial inclusion has transformed this landscape across the country. "Today in India, digital banking has connected everyone to 24-hour banking services,” observed PM Modi.
"Today, through digital banking, every family in the country has become a beneficiary,” asserted Shri Modi. The Prime Minister highlighted the complete elimination of any leakages today. He explained that every single rupee disbursed by the central government now reaches the beneficiary's account intact. "This has become possible only because of the nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts opened in the country,” noted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that even individuals without collateral can now access affordable formal credit to start businesses, the Prime Minister highlighted how small entrepreneurs, traditional artisans, street vendors, and unorganized workers are thriving through targeted interventions. He noted that 13 crore people became first-time entrepreneurs under the Mudra Yojana, lakhs of street vendors and skilled artisans gained formal credit via PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma, and Self-Help Groups representing 10 crore rural women received thousands of crores in bank assistance. "For the first time, they have received the benefit of formal banking,” observed Shri Modi.
Noting that debit and credit cards were once the exclusive preserve of the wealthy before becoming accessible to every citizen through crores of RuPay cards symbolizing self-respect and self-reliance, the Prime Minister credited the banking fraternity for driving this transformation. He lauded the collective efforts of the central bank, commercial banks, and every single banking employee across the nation. "All of you are partners in this glory,” commended PM Modi.
Detailing the unprecedented expansion of the social security net alongside economic empowerment guided by the mantra of Nagrik Devo Bhava, the Prime Minister noted that the Atal Pension Yojana covers 9 crore citizens, including 38 lakh in Odisha, while the PM Suraksha Bima Yojana, at a 20-rupee annual premium for a 2-lakh-rupee accident cover, and the PM Jeevan Jyoti Yojana, at under 450 rupees annually for life cover, have made once-luxury insurance accessible to the poor and middle class. He pointed out that unlike other governments that would have generated major headlines and fanfare over such payouts, over 25,000 crore rupees in claims have been quietly disbursed to families during difficult times. “This is what good governance is,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Stating that while the past decade focused on banking the unbanked, the coming decade is dedicated to making banking more efficient and reliable with the support of Odisha's new Data Centre and robust computing systems, the Prime Minister warned that modern warfare targets economies through evolving cyber threats. Stressing that a rising economic power must shield its financial system from cyber looters and cyber terrorists, he emphasized the need to replace outdated training tools with modern infrastructure and skilled human resources. "Right here, the role of this new cybersecurity institute becomes crucial,” asserted PM Modi.
Spotlighting Eastern India as a powerful growth engine for a Viksit Bharat and noting the accelerated momentum under Odisha's current government, the Prime Minister observed that the state is pairing its traditional mineral-based industries with a new ecosystem of semiconductors, electronics, data centres, and advanced computing to script a new future from mines to microchips. Expressing full confidence that these emerging avenues will unlock vast opportunities and fulfill the grand dreams of Odisha's youth, he concluded with his festive best wishes and chants of Jai Jagannath. "You will see, Odisha, from mines to microchips, is going to write a new future,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during inauguration of RBI facilities in Bhubaneswar, Odisha
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 OCT 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Jai Jagannath.
Governor of Odisha, Shri Brajmohan Ram ji; popular Chief Minister of the state, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi ji; my colleagues in the Union Government, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman ji, Shri Jual Oram ji; Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, Shri Sanjay Malhotra ji; Deputy Chief Ministers of Odisha, Smt. Pravati Parida ji, Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo ji; distinguished guests associated with the banking and financial sector, ladies and gentlemen.
Why is the atmosphere so serious? Does banking carry this much pressure, does technology carry this much pressure? Please sit comfortably.
With the blessings of Mahaprabhu, today Bhubaneswar is giving a new institution to a New India. The inauguration of both the RBI's Data Centre and the Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar marks an important occasion. This is going to be of immense benefit to the people of Odisha and the entire country. I extend my heartiest congratulations to the RBI and everyone associated with this project.
Friends,
Today's programme bears testimony to how the approach to governance in India is transforming and how rapidly it is evolving. And our focus within this is: priority of development, expansion of development, and reaching the last person with development.
Friends,
After independence, large cities were developed in the country, grand institutions were established, large hospitals were built, and massive airports were constructed. Yet, a vast section of the country kept waiting for basic amenities. Delhi had large hospitals, but people in smaller cities and remote areas had to travel long distances for better medical treatment. Large cities enjoyed air travel facilities, but connecting smaller towns with air connectivity was not given adequate focus. Big cities had some amenities, whereas in numerous villages, meeting basic needs such as roads, electricity, and water remained a formidable challenge. Railway stations formed the most crucial link of the common citizen's travel, yet modern amenities were lacking at these stations. In other words, ensuring that the benefits of development reached every region and every citizen equally remained a major hurdle. We made an effort to transform this very mindset. We proceeded with a model of Pro-People, Pro-Active, Good Governance. For us, development denotes balanced progress across India - opportunities for villages as well as smaller towns. Our goal is to extend better connectivity to far-flung areas, provide facilities for underprivileged families to live with dignity, and continually instill confidence in every citizen that they will not be left behind in the journey of development. Today, the nation's expressways are linking smaller cities. Premier institutions like AIIMS have expanded across multiple states. Medical colleges are being opened in smaller towns. Nearly 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been established in villages. Digital connectivity is expanding into remote regions. This is the true purpose of governance now: making citizens' lives easier and offering new avenues for their
aspirations.
Friends,
Our banking sector has also stood as a prime example of how ordinary families, the poor, and the middle class were kept deprived for decades. In the 1960s and 70s, banks were nationalised in the name of the poor. Yet, until 2014, more than half of the country's population was excluded from the banking ecosystem. Financial products such as bank loans were a distant dream even for the middle class; the poor, small farmers, the landless, and our sisters and daughters could not even fathom accessing them. Today, digital banking in India has connected everyone to 24-hour financial services. But prior to 2014, there was an entirely different era of 'phone banking'. A select few in Delhi and those connected with influential circles were granted loans worth thousands of crores through phone calls. Poor and middle-class families required a guarantor merely to open a single bank account, whereas under the Congress's phone banking arrangement, thousands of crores of rupees were available anytime for the wealthy. It was the consequence of this very mismanagement that pushed India's banking system into the grip of NPAs, driving it to the brink of ruin.
Friends,
For any substantial transformation, having an expansive mindset is essential; when intentions are pure and motives are noble, tasks that seem impossible turn into reality. Where vision is narrow, possibilities also shrink. The frameworks built by the nation in recent years, along with the new ecosystem developed under Digital India, have extended banking to every single citizen. Today, India's banking sector stands among the strongest in the world. Earlier, through phone banking, only those with access to a privileged family in Delhi benefited. Today, through digital banking, every household across the nation has become a beneficiary.
Friends,
It was from this very land of Odisha that a former Prime Minister of the country once stated that when one rupee is sent from Delhi, only 15 paise reaches the people. That was a statement from a Prime Minister. That was one era, and this is today. Today, when one rupee leaves Delhi, the entire one rupee reaches the bank account of every beneficiary. As Nirmala ji mentioned just now, this has been made possible solely because of the approximately 59 to 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts opened in the country.
Friends,
Today, even someone who has nothing to offer the bank as a guarantee is able to secure an affordable and accessible loan to start their own work. From small entrepreneurs to traditional artisans, from street vendors to workers in the unorganised sector, they have received the benefits of formal banking for the first time. Through the Mudra Yojana, 13 crore people have become first-time entrepreneurs. PM SVANidhi has provided loans to lakhs of street vendors for the first time. The PM Vishwakarma scheme has connected lakhs of skilled craftspersons with banks. Banks have also extended assistance worth thousands of crores of rupees to self-help groups comprising 10 crore rural women.
Friends,
This is the same nation where debit and credit cards were once symbols reserved for the wealthy. Today, they are accessible to every citizen. Crores of RuPay credit and debit cards have been issued in the country, becoming symbols of both self-respect and self-reliance. All of this has been achieved through your collective cooperation. Be it the RBI, every bank in the nation, or each bank employee serving within them - the work you have accomplished makes you truly deserving of this success.
Friends,
Over the past decade, alongside financial empowerment, the social security net has witnessed an unprecedented expansion. Through the Atal Pension Yojana, 9 crore people have received social security coverage, with 38 lakh individuals covered in Odisha alone. About 10 to 12 years ago, insurance was considered a luxury; the poor and middle class could hardly contemplate it. For us, ‘Nagrik Devo Bhava’ (The Citizen is Divine) is the guiding mantra of good governance. To provide protection during accidents, we introduced the PM Suraksha Bima Yojana. At a nominal premium of just ₹20 per year, an insurance coverage of up to ₹2 lakh is being provided. Similarly, for life insurance, we introduced the PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, available at an annual premium of less than ₹450. Crores of Indians are enrolled in both these schemes. To date, claims exceeding ₹25,000 crore have been disbursed to the public. If any other government had announced the distribution of ₹25,000 crore, it would have generated massive headlines, accompanied by celebrations and fanfares for months. However, under our administration, this support reaches the poor and the middle class during difficult times silently and without fanfare. This is what defines good governance.
Friends,
The past decade focused on extending banking access to those who were excluded. The coming decade belongs to making banking more efficient and more dependable. In this effort, this new Data Centre in Odisha will play a major role. If we are to keep the banking system secure, its digital infrastructure must also remain protected. For this reason, we require robust data centres and empowered computing systems.
And friends,
We all understand that modern warfare is not waged solely with weapons. Weakening a country can also be attempted by striking at its economy. As India gains financial strength, safeguarding our banking system against cyber criminals and cyber terrorists is equally imperative. The nature of cyber threats is evolving today. We cannot counter such emerging challenges using outdated systems, obsolete training modules, or legacy tools. This necessitates modern infrastructure alongside skilled human resources. It is precisely here that the role of this new Cybersecurity Training Institute becomes critically important.
Friends,
These new facilities of the RBI also reflect a fresh priority for India. Eastern India is emerging as a powerful growth engine for a developed India. Following the formation of the double-engine government in Odisha, progress has gained new momentum. Alongside its natural resources, Odisha's economy is now being fortified by technology. On one hand, mineral-based industries are expanding; on the other hand, concerted efforts are underway to foster a new ecosystem for semiconductors and electronics. You will witness that Odisha is set to script a new future, spanning from mines to microchips. Fresh investment prospects are emerging in Odisha across data centres and advanced computing, opening numerous avenues for its youth. I assure the young people of Odisha that the big dreams you have envisioned will certainly be fulfilled. We will do it; we are determined to accomplish this. With this spirit, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you.
Best wishes to everyone.
Jai Jagannath!

title: English rendering of PM’s address in the 139th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 25.10.2026
date:
Posted On:

content:
My dear countrymen,
Welcome once again to ‘Mann Ki Baat’. Twelve years ago, on the pious occasion of Vijayadashami, we began ‘Mann Ki Baat’. Since then, this journey of our’s has continued without a break. You are both my fellow travellers and my guides on this path. Friends, for me, ‘Mann Ki Baat’ has been an auspicious opportunity to proudly celebrate the hard work, valour, commitment, dedication, and spirit of service of the common people of our nation. Our country has had a long-standing tradition of Teerth Yatra. ‘Mann Ki Baat’ is, for me, nothing less than a pilgrimage - a journey to closely understand the efforts of our people and to salute their contributions. Friends, those who live for society and the nation are, in themselves, like a ‘Teerth’. Over these 12 years, many individuals from every corner of the country have come to the fore - people whose extraordinary work often goes unnoticed by society at large. ‘Mann Ki Baat’ has served to bring such countless, inspiring stories to all of you.
Friends,
Through this program, I am, in a sense, paying obeisance to the ‘collective strength of the people’; Lok-Shakti of our nation. It provides me with an opportunity to connect with every family across the country. I receive hundreds of messages in which people share that listening to ‘Mann Ki Baat’ makes them feel as though I am amidst them - like a member of their own family - engaging in a conversation. For me, this deep connection and the affection shown by all of you - my listeners - is a priceless treasure.
My dear countrymen,
Our nation possesses many traditional skills that have been a part of our identity for generations. And it is heartening to see that these traditions are now being integrated with diverse, innovative approaches, allowing them to evolve and remain relevant to the present day. One such initiative has been underway in Punjab for some time; an organization called ‘Kheti Virasat Mission’ has begun to breathe new life into organic farming and traditional agricultural practices. The team aimed to promote natural cotton cultivation in the Malwa region of Punjab. This initiative was named ‘Nav-Trinjan’.
Under this project, organic cotton is grown there without the use of any chemicals. They also cultivate cotton that possesses natural colors, eliminating the need for additional chemicals to dye the resulting yarn or fabric. You can imagine what a significant contribution this makes towards protecting the environment.
Friends,
A few years ago, ‘Nav-Trinjan’ also established a weaving school with the goal of passing on the craft of weaving to the next generation. This school has transformed the lives of many women. Ramandeep Kaur ji is one such example; she previously worked as a labourer, but following her training at the school, she is now recognized as a skilled weaver. Rekha Rani ji had never even seen a handloom before undergoing training; a shawl woven by her has been presented to the Honorable President of India. Similarly, Suneha Devi ji, who once worked as a domestic help, is now creating exquisite fabrics on a handloom. Rajni Kaur ji, who once depended on manual labour in the fields, has found that her new skills have significantly helped her in supporting her household.
Following training from the school, many such women are now crafting shawls, towels, and other textiles using yarn made from indigenous organic cotton. These efforts are bringing prosperity to their lives. A few months ago, on National Handloom Day, I too had the opportunity to meet this team. During that, I experienced their passion and dedication towards their work. I extend my heartfelt best wishes to the entire team for a bright future.
My dear countrymen,
We have had a long-standing tradition of respecting nature. Our ancestors taught us that maintaining cleanliness in our surroundings and caring for water sources is our own responsibility. It brings me great joy to see so many people across the country embodying this spirit. The same sentiment can also be seen in the Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand. There, people have come together in an effort to breathe new life into a river - the 'Heval' river. Some time ago, the water level in the Heval river began to decline… the natural water sources in the surrounding area were also drying up. In this scenario, the local administration and the villagers joined forces to launch a campaign to save the Heval river.
Measures were undertaken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge and plant a large number of trees. Today, thanks to these efforts, the Heval river has been revitalized and simultaneously dozens of natural water sources have received help in their restoration.
Friends,
When a society unites imbuing such a spirit, change is definitely guaranteed. We can see a glimpse of that in our festivals as well. In just a few days, the auspicious festivals of Diwali and Chhath are approaching; For that, cleanliness drives are being run at many places. It is essential that we maintain the cleanliness of the places where we live. Only our small, individual efforts can bring about significant change in our surroundings.
My dear countrymen,
During this festive season, you must have noticed a shift in your surroundings. People are now placing great importance on Swadeshi products while shopping. This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is now taking our products to global markets.
For instance, *makhana* from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and *arhar dal* from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives - meaning, new global markets are opening up for India's farmers. Friends, while discussing local products, I would like to draw your attention to another important aspect: the packaging of a product is just as significant as its quality. Often, when we see an item in the market, it is its attractive packaging that draws us to pick it up. We want to know about a product just by looking at its packaging. Realizing that, there is now an increasing emphasis on packaging.
Friends,
In Maharashtra, tribal communities have placed a strong focus on the packaging of the products they create. There, through an initiative called ‘Shabari Naturals,’ products like honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo-based items are being brought to the market - their packaging reflects tribal art. You will be pleased to know that this packaging has received Japan’s prestigious ‘Good Design Award.’ Our youth are also experimenting anew in this field; a ‘bamboo’ start-up in Karnataka is creating packaging material from bamboo and agricultural residue.
Friends,
When we talk about local products, it is only natural to mention Khadi. This time on Gandhi Jayanti, sales of the products of Khadi Gram Udyog exceeded ₹28 crore in a single day. It is an increase of ₹1.5 crore over the previous year. This means that the popularity of Khadi continues to grow, and the benefits are reaching those whose skills and hard work bring items like Khadi and various handicrafts to life.
Friends,
During the festive season, we often buy many things for our families and loved ones. This time too, do prioritize products made by local artisans when you shop; your purchases will boost their morale. This sense of affection will further strengthen the ‘Vocal for Local’ movement. As this movement gains momentum, the dream of ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ will be realized all the faster. For that, I personally urge you to prioritize and highlight products crafted by local artisans.
My dear countrymen,
There’s a remarkable trait of our people… we quickly embrace new technology. We naturally integrate technology into our daily lives - the ‘e-Sanjeevani’ yojana is an excellent example of that. This demonstrates how technology can be effectively utilized to make people's lives easier. It gives me great satisfaction to note that approximately 50 crore tele-consultations have been conducted through this platform so far – It is a massive figure. It serves as an excellent testament to the power of technology, the dedicated spirit of our doctors, and the trust placed in the system by our countrymen.
Friends,
Today, through its extensive network, the 'e-Sanjeevani' service has reached even the remotest corners of the country. The stories of those who have benefited from it will make you emotional. In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Oho-Tahane, from the Jarawa tribe on Baratang Island, was suffering from a high fever… breathing too was getting difficult. Amid that, local health workers used e-Sanjeevani to consult an expert doctor. The child had pneumonia; once he came under the care of the expert doctor, his condition began to improve rapidly.
Friends,
In Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, a man named Kunhi Koya—around 60 years of age - suddenly fell ill. Through e-Sanjeevani, contact was established with an experienced doctor located across the sea in Kavaratti. That experienced doctor provided guidance to the local medical team, which helped bring relief to Kunhi Koya. In Zanskar, Ladakh, Kunjang Dolma experienced some complications during her pregnancy; during that situation, e-Sanjeevani worked for her, allowing a specialist doctor to provide immediate assistance. In Peren, Nagaland, a 12-year-old boy named Mushem suffered from an ear infection and fever; he, too, benefited from e-Sanjeevani… The expert doctor was able to promptly diagnose his condition and recommend the appropriate medication.
Friends,
There was a time when even a simple health check-up or a visit to a doctor would take a long time and involve significant hardship. Today, nearly 190,000 'Ayushman Arogya Mandirs' across the country have brought new facilities into people's lives. These Arogya Mandirs are in a way, evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats.
It’s most heartening to know that, people in rural areas are now undergoing regular health check-ups to stay healthy, in which 'e-Sanjeevani' is playing a vital role.
My dear countrymen,
Earlier this month, I visited Chennai. There I met many of the nation's scientists, researchers, and young talents. Our youth are currently working on subjects that have the potential to transform the future of all humanity; one such field is 'Brain Research.' In that connection, I inaugurated the 'Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre' at IIT Madras. This centre has developed a brain-imaging technology platform that serves as a global benchmark. Through that, high-resolution, digital 3D images of the human brain, are being created, with the goal of mapping and studying 100 human brains in minute detail. This is the first mission of its kind in the world, and it utilizes the 'Param Shakti' supercomputer.
Friends,
The nation's industry has played a significant role, in collaboration with the government, in establishing this brain centre. Many IIT alumni and academia have also come together to support this research centre. This project is of immense importance because, despite significant scientific progress, the human brain remains a major scientific enigma. Even in the present day, conditions like Alzheimer's and Dementia still lack a definitive cure. Therefore, the deeper our scientific understanding of how the human brain functions, the more new scope will be created in the future. It has also been decided that this data from 100 human brains will be made available as an open-source resource for research across various fields.
Friends,
Organ donation plays a vital role in such advanced research. Those who choose to donate their organs after their lifetime not only save the lives of many others but also make research possible. One such example is that of Shivani-ji from Narmadapuram in Madhya Pradesh.
Shivani ji had met with a road accident; while this brought a great tragedy upon her family, even in such a difficult time, they made a decision that serves as an inspiration to us all - the decision was to donate Shivani ji’s organs. This choice by Shivani ji’s family sends a powerful message to society and the nation. Such a step of humanity can bring happiness back into a family’s life, while also providing significant support to research efforts.
My dear countrymen,
I would also like to share some other experiences from my visit to Chennai. The first was my interaction with young people on the metro, while another was my visit to IIT Madras. It was truly heartening to see how our youth are working on innovative solutions to problems. One of the start-ups I met focuses on verifying the quality of gold, which can help prevent fraud in gold purchases. Another team of young people is developing a platform that could enable the rapid recovery of funds lost to bank fraud. Meanwhile, another team is exploring how AI can assist in the screening for cervical cancer.
Friends,
The interaction at IIT was entirely focused on 'deep-tech.' These start-ups are being supported by the incubation ecosystem at IIT Madras. Among them is a start-up that is developing an electric vehicle capable of flying over the sea. Another start-up is developing fast-charging batteries for drones and electric vehicles. One team is working on the application of AI in defence technology.
Friends, our youth are achieving such extraordinary things today because they are receiving the right environment and support. It is not as if there has ever been a shortage of talent in our country. In just a few days, on October 31st, we will mark the 100th birth anniversary of one such great Indian scientist, Narinder Singh Kapany. The world knows him as the 'Father of Fiber Optics.' He was born in the Moga district of Punjab. His advanced research into the technology of transmitting light through thin fibers lent a new direction to the world of communication. It is difficult to even imagine the era of internet and digital communication that we live in today without fiber optics.
On this occasion, we pay our respects to Narinder Singh Kapany. I would like our youth to read and learn about scientists like him, and draw inspiration from them.
Friends,
Just in a few days, the 31st of October marks the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel - a day the nation observes as 'Ekta Diwas'. On this occasion, a 'Run for Unity' is organized across the country. ‘Run For Unity’ offers a significant opportunity to strengthen our unity and reaffirm our commitment to the nation. I urge all of you to participate enthusiastically in this year’s 'Run for Unity' and to bring along your family, friends, and those around you.
Friends,
You may recall that, at India’s call, 2023 was celebrated as the 'International Year of Millets.' It received a very positive response globally. Through this initiative, people discovered how deeply the superfood 'Shree Anna' i.e. millets - are rooted in our own culture. In the North-East, too, there has long been a rich tradition of millet cultivation; however, over time, people had begun to drift away from it. Now, that situation is changing.
Friends,
In the West Jaintia Hills district of Meghalaya, there is a village called Khanduli. Over many generations, millets have been an integral part of the local food culture there. Yet, for some time, the number of farmers cultivating them had been on the decline. Amid that, two women friends from the village undertook a new initiative: they focused on creating new products from millets. Lending value addition to these grains, they developed items such as cookies, cakes, and muffins, as well as baby food. This led to an increase in the sales of millet-based products and a subsequent rise in the demand for millets themselves. Amid that, farmers there have also begun cultivating millets once again. Friends, in the village of Sadolpara, located in the West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya, some new initiatives are underway. A local farmer there, Chekjing Sangma, recognizing the importance of millets, has started cultivating them using modern methods. This has not only increased his income but has also fostered greater awareness within the village. Similarly, there is a village called Kezoma in Kohima, Nagaland, where the cultivation of millets had ceased for over a decade.
As a result, an entire generation grew up unfamiliar with this traditional crop - imagine… a crop once grown by their own grandparents, was being forgotten by the villagers themselves. In 2024, the local community resumed the cultivation of millets, and in 2025, Kezoma celebrated its first-ever millet festival. Now, there is a rapidly growing demand for products made from millets in this region as well.
Friends,
Examples related to millet cultivation carry a significant message. These examples demonstrate how our youth are linking traditional crops with new opportunities, and how our villages are advancing on the path to prosperity while preserving their heritage.
My dear countrymen,
Tomorrow, October 26th, marks the birth anniversary of Maharishi Valmiki. Though thousands of years have passed, the Ramayan, of Maharishi Valmiki ji, continues to offer us new insights even today.
Through the Ramayan, Maharishi Valmiki has imparted profound life lessons to us… on the one hand he emphasizes the value of persistent effort; on the other he also highlights the importance of service, compassion, and social harmony. In the Valmiki Ramayan, the character of Bhagwan Ram serves as a beautiful embodiment of these values – Bhagwan Ram embraced the love and devotion of Mata Shabari… honored his friendship with Nishadraj. The spirit of taking everyone along - these ideals continue to guide us even today. This sentiment is also reflected in the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, where shrines dedicated to Maharishi Valmiki, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari as well have been built. I am pleased that the airport in Ayodhya has also been named after Maharishi Valmiki. These initiatives enrich our great tradition - the very tradition that places the highest value on service, social harmony, and compassion.
My dear countrymen,
The soil of India has given birth to many such great personalities who have left an indelible mark. One such great figure is Bhai Parmanand ji. In a few days, on November 4th, we will celebrate his 150th birth anniversary.
A major source of inspiration and ideals for Bhai Parmanand ji was his deep association with Arya Samaj. In the very early 20th century, he traveled to South Africa for the work of Arya Samaj, where he also met revered Bapu. He also worked among the 'Girmitiya' community in Guyana, which was a significant centre for Arya Samaj at that time. During my own visit to Guyana, I had the privilege of visiting the Arya Samaj memorial.
Friends,
Bhai Parmanand ji played a major role in the freedom movement. It is said that it was Bhai Parmanand ji who had persuaded Lala Har Dayal ji to go to America. He was also one of the founding members of the Ghadar Party. His influence on the struggle for independence was so profound that the British authorities sentenced him to 'Kala Pani'. He authored a book titled 'Aapbeeti: Kaale Paani Ki Kaaraavaas Kahaani'. This book is a must-read to truly understand the sacrifices made by freedom fighters. After completing his sentence, Bhai Parmanand ji turned his focus towards the field of education. You might be surprised to learn that he even taught Veer Bhagat Singh.
In later years, he remained associated with the Hindu Mahasabha for many years as well. In other words, from his connection to Gandhiji to his time in Guyana, and from the Ghadar movement to the Andamans, his personality stands as a great source of inspiration. I offer my respectful homage to Bhai Parmanand ji. I urge the youth to learn about them and inspire others as well.
My dear countrymen,
The coming days will be filled with the festive spirit of Diwali, the great festival of Chhath, and several other celebrations. Do celebrate these festivals with your entire family while staying healthy and safe and include others in your joy. I extend my best wishes to all of you for the upcoming festivals.
As always, I look forward to receiving your messages and suggestions. Your suggestions provide new topics and new direction to ‘Mann Ki Baat’. We shall meet again next month, with new endeavors and inspiring stories from our fellow countrymen.
Thank you very much.
Namaskar.

INDIAN AND RUSSIAN PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATIONS DISCUSS STRENGTHENING COOPERATION AT GLOBAL FORA AND COLLECTIVE EFFORTS TO COMBAT TERRORISM

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ALSO MEETS PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATIONS FROM CUBA, EGYPT AND BELARUS
date:
Posted On:
                25 OCT 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Parliament of India is all set to host 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on 26 October 2026.
Ahead of the two day Forum, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla held a bilateral meeting with the Parliamentary Delegation from Russia, led by H.E. Mr. Vyacheslav Volodin, Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation.
During the meeting, Indian and Russian Parliamentary Delegations underscored the need for strengthening cooperation at global fora and collective efforts to combat terrorism. Extending a warm welcome to Mr. Volodin and his Delegation on behalf of the Parliament of India and 1.4 billion Indians, Shri Birla highlighted the special and time-tested friendship between India and Russia, rooted in mutual trust, respect and shared aspirations. He also appreciated Russia’s consistent support for India in its fight against terrorism and stressed that the international community must demonstrate unity and resolve towards terrorism, and work together for global peace. Noting that the two countries would complete 80 years of diplomatic relations in 2027, he emphasised that the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership has been further strengthened under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin.
Emphasising on the importance of parliamentary diplomacy, Shri Birla called for sustained institutional engagement between Lok Sabha and the State Duma through regular meetings of the India-Russia Inter-Parliamentary Commission and exchanges of parliamentary delegations, particularly young and women parliamentarians.
Referring to India's BRICS Presidency in 2026, Shri Birla emphasised the importance of a people-centric approach and sought Russia's active participation in strengthening cooperation among BRICS Parliaments. He highlighted the need for collective efforts to address contemporary global challenges, including climate change and terrorism, and underscored the importance of making international institutions more responsive to changing global circumstances. Shri Birla also reiterated the need for reforms of the United Nations Security Council and conveyed his appreciation for Russia's continued support for India's permanent membership of the Council.
During the meeting, Shri Birla also highlighted opportunities for further strengthening bilateral cooperation in nuclear energy, industry and other sectors. Underscoring the importance of cultural exchanges and people-to-people contacts as vital pillars of bilateral relations, he observed that the deep affection and goodwill shared by the peoples of India and Russia provide a strong foundation for further expanding cooperation.
Noting the growing scope of cooperation in trade, industry and agriculture, Chairman of the State Duma H.E. Mr. Vyacheslav Volodin stressed on the need to promote joint business ventures and remove obstacles to bilateral trade and investment. He also underscored the importance of regular exchanges between the State Duma and the Parliament of India, including through multilateral platforms such as BRICS. He reaffirmed Russia's commitment to strengthening cooperation in cultural and humanitarian spheres and enhancing people-to-people exchanges. Expressing confidence in the future of India-Russia relations, he observed that sustained parliamentary engagement and closer cooperation across diverse sectors would contribute to further deepening the longstanding partnership between the two countries.
Later in the day, Shri Birla met Parliamentary Delegations from Cuba, Egypt and Belarus and engaged in mutually enriching and productive discussions.
On Monday, the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi would grace the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations.
The Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development.” It would facilitate consensus-based dialogue through four high-level sessions themed on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.
In addition, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of the parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices.
Alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme. The Vice-President of India will host a banquet in honour of the distinguished guests.
The conference will conclude on 27 October, 2026.
Had a warm and fruitful meeting with H.E. Mr Vyacheslav Volodin, Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation, ahead of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum 2026.

The enduring bonds of friendship, mutual trust and understanding between India and Russia form the bedrock of our longstanding partnership. As our two nations mark 80 years of diplomatic relations, we reaffirmed our commitment to further deepening the India–Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership, rooted in mutual respect, trust and shared aspirations.

We discussed expanding parliamentary cooperation through sustained institutional engagement between Lok Sabha and the State Duma, regular exchanges of parliamentary delegations, and greater interaction among young and women parliamentarians. I also shared India’s initiatives to leverage technology, including Sansad Bhashini, to make parliamentary proceedings more accessible, inclusive and citizen-centric. We also exchanged views on strengthening cooperation among BRICS Parliaments, combating terrorism through concerted international efforts, and advancing reforms of the United Nations Security Council. I conveyed my appreciation for Russia’s continued support for India’s permanent membership of the Council.

I am confident that stronger parliamentary engagement will impart fresh momentum to our time-tested partnership, further reinforcing the deep-rooted friendship and close ties between India and Russia.

title: CCPA Intensifies Action Against Misleading Advertisements and Non-Compliant Sale of Walkie-Talkies
subtitle:
CCPA Imposes ₹1 Lakh Penalty on Hogar Technologies and Innovations LLP for Misleading Advertisements of Walkie-Talkies

Over 16,970 non-compliant listings identified across online platforms; notices issued to 13 e-commerce entities

Advertisements must clearly disclose operating frequencies, licensing requirements and other essential regulatory information to enable informed consumer decisions

CCPA has passed final orders against 12 entities, imposing cumulative penalties of ₹58 lakh for misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices relating to walkie-talkies
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 OCT 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of
₹1 lakh on M/s Hogar Technologies and Innovations LLP
for misleading advertisements and product listings of walkie-talkies that failed to disclose essential regulatory information, including operating frequencies and applicable licensing requirements. The order was passed by the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Smt. Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Shri Anupam Mishra, under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
The action forms part of the CCPA’s ongoing enforcement measures against misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices relating to the listing, advertisement and sale of walkie-talkies (Personal Mobile Radios) across online platforms and websites.
CCPA finds inadequate disclosure of regulatory requirements
In its latest order, the CCPA examined advertisements and product listings of various walkie-talkie models displayed on the website of M/s Hogar Technologies and Innovations LLP. The Authority observed that the listings did not clearly disclose the operating frequencies of the devices, applicable licensing requirements and regulatory approvals. Such omissions could mislead consumers into believing that the devices could be legally operated without obtaining the requisite regulatory authorisations.
Under the
Use of Low Power and Very Low Power Short Range Radio Frequency Devices (Exemption from Licensing Requirement) Rules, 2018
, personal mobile radios operating within the prescribed frequency range of
446.0–446.2 MHz
are exempt from the requirement of obtaining a licence, subject to applicable conditions. Other wireless radio frequency devices operating outside the exempted frequency range are subject to the relevant regulatory requirements.
During the proceedings, the company submitted that it possessed a valid Dealer Possessing Licence (DPL) and that the devices were covered by applicable Equipment Type Approval (ETA) certifications. It also contended that its website was primarily intended for informational and lead-generation purposes and did not facilitate direct online transactions.
After examining the company’s submissions, investigation findings and material available on record, the CCPA observed that
possession of regulatory approvals does not absolve an advertiser of its obligation to provide accurate, complete and material information to consumers at the pre-purchase stage
.
Website-based product promotions also subject to consumer protection requirements
The CCPA further observed that the absence of an online payment gateway or shopping cart facility does not exclude promotional representations made through a website from the ambit of misleading advertisements under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Advertisements and product listings
must provide adequate information regarding applicable regulatory requirements,
irrespective of the mode through which the products are ultimately sold.
The Authority noted that omission of material information concerning operating frequencies and licensing requirements was likely to mislead consumers about the conditions under which the advertised devices could lawfully be operated. Such omissions could expose consumers to potential legal and financial consequences and undermine their ability to make informed purchasing decisions.
Accordingly, the CCPA found the conduct of M/s Hogar Technologies and Innovations LLP to be in violation of the relevant provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, relating to misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices.
CCPA’s action against online listings of walkie-talkies
The CCPA had earlier taken
suo motu
cognisance of the large-scale listing and sale of walkie-talkies on e-commerce platforms without mandatory regulatory disclosures. During its examination,
over 16,970 non-compliant listings
were identified across platforms, and notices were issued to 13 e-commerce entities, including Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Meta (Facebook Marketplace), JioMart, IndiaMART and TradeIndia, among others.
The Authority has so far passed final orders against
12 entities, imposing cumulative penalties of ₹58 lakh
for misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices relating to walkie-talkies. These include penalties of ₹10 lakh each on Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd., Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd., Meesho Pvt. Ltd., Meta Platforms and TradeIndia (Infocom Network Pvt. Ltd.), and ₹1 lakh each on JioMart (Reliance Retail Ltd.), Chimiya, MaskMan Toys, Talk Pro (Iconet Services Pvt. Ltd.), Sanchar Wireless Communications Ltd., Antriksh Technosys Pvt. Ltd. and Hogar Technologies and Innovations LLP.
Certain entities have challenged the orders and proceedings initiated by the CCPA before judicial forums. Amazon Seller Services Pvt. Ltd. and Flipkart Internet Pvt. Ltd. have approached the Hon’ble Karnataka High Court challenging the orders passed by the Authority. Meta Platforms and TradeIndia (Infocom Network Pvt. Ltd.) have approached the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) against the orders imposing penalties of ₹10 lakh each. In the case of TradeIndia, the NCDRC has directed the company to deposit the penalty amount. IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd. has also approached the Hon’ble Delhi High Court challenging the proceedings initiated by the CCPA, while the matter remains under consideration before the Authority.
CCPA reiterates the importance of transparent regulatory disclosures
The CCPA reiterated that advertisements and product listings of walkie-talkies must clearly disclose operating frequencies, applicable licensing requirements and other material regulatory information to enable consumers to make informed decisions. Such disclosures are particularly important for products whose lawful use is subject to specific regulatory conditions.
The Authority reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding consumer interests, preventing misleading advertisements and addressing unfair trade practices, particularly in relation to products involving regulatory compliance and public safety considerations.
The final order is available on the CCPA website:
https://ccpa.doca.gov.in/

title: NIFTEM-K Hosts India’s First AI × Food Tech Hackathon, ‘Hack the Fork’
date:
Posted On:
                25 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management, Kundli (NIFTEM-K), hosted Hack the Fork, India’s first AI × Food Tech Hackathon focused on leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) to address real-world challenges in the alternative protein industry. The 24-hour hackathon was inaugurated by Ms. Alice Pjie, Director, Hack the Fork, on October 24 and concluded on October 25, with participating teams presenting their innovative solutions before an expert jury.
Organised by Hack the Fork, a France-based non-profit initiative, in collaboration with NIFTEM-K, the event aimed to bring together young innovators, researchers and technology enthusiasts to explore AI-driven solutions for sustainable food systems. From an initial pool of over 85 applicant teams, 25 teams were shortlisted for the final round. Of these, 22 teams from 10 states, comprising over 90 participants, participated in the intensive innovation challenge at the institute. The participants represented diverse disciplines and institutions, including IITs, IIITs and the University of Delhi.
Dr. Harinder Singh Oberoi, Director, NIFTEM-K, highlighted the significance of India's first AI × Food Tech Hackathon in generating innovative ideas and strengthening the country's food ecosystem. He expressed confidence that the initiative would encourage creative thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration and the development of technology-driven solutions to address emerging challenges in the food sector. Dr. Oberoi also congratulated all participating teams for their enthusiasm, creativity and commitment to innovation. He encouraged the young innovators to make the most of this opportunity, explore new possibilities and develop practical solutions that could contribute to a stronger, more sustainable and future-ready food-processing ecosystem.
The event was coordinated by Dr. Vimal Pant, Professor at NIFTEM-K and CEO of NTIBIF. content:
In a lethal blow against drugs by Modi Government, NCB launches ‘Operation Trident’, with 38 teams striking 38 locations simultaneously across Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur. The crackdown is in line with Modi Govt’s policy of Zero Tolerance against Drugs and strategic shift from a seizure-centric to a network-centric approach. The massive three-state multiagency blitzkrieg was launched against transnational narco-financial syndicates across Assam, Mizoram and Manipur. In line with Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029), Operation exemplifies shift from a seizure-centric to a network-centric and financial disruption approach to uproot transnational syndicates.
In a post on X platform, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said “Modi govt’s lethal blows against drugs continue...Our agencies launched a barrage of simultaneous crackdowns across 38 locations in Assam, Mizoram and Manipur on 23 October, smashing an international narco-cartel. The operation revealed ₹100 crore worth of hawala transactions, froze 1,424 bank accounts, attached properties worth ₹17.82 crore, seized 500 detonators and ₹12 lakh in cash, and led to the arrest of 18 people.
The network trafficked narcotics across the borders of India, Myanmar and Bangladesh through the Death Triangle Corridor. The offensive attests to India’s Himalayan resolve to realise the mission of eradicating every drug network by 31 December 2029. India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels. Heartiest congratulations to the anti-narcotics team comprising central agencies, and police forces of the three states.”
‘OPERATION TRIDENT’
Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) spearheaded “Operation Trident” in the early hours of 23 October 2026. In an extraordinary demonstration of multi-agency synergy, the NCB, in seamless coordination with Mizoram Police and Enforcement Directorate (ED) launched a massive, simultaneous crack-down to dismantle the operational and financial backbone of a major transnational drug trafficking cartel. Meticulous Multi-Agency Planning & Synchronised Execution Operation Trident represents a benchmark in institutional cohesion in intelligence sharing & operational planning to target drug kingpins & their associates in Mizoram. Preceded by days of covert intelligence fusion, joint target-mapping, and high-level tactical briefings among central and state enforcement agencies, the operation was meticulously designed to simultaneously strike both the logistics nodes and the illicit financial arteries of the syndicates.
Acting with surgical precision under a unified command structure, 38 multi-agency composite teams were mobilised concurrently across 38 pre-identified locations spanning the three North-Eastern states of Assam, Mizoram, and Manipur. The coordinated strikes extensively covered key urban hubs and sensitive border corridors—including Aizawl, Champhai, and the strategic Indo-
Myanmar border trading town of Zokhawthar in Mizoram, alongside linked operative bases in Churachandpur, Manipur and the Cachar/Assam transit corridor. Despite challenging terrain and vast geographical spread, exceptional inter-departmental coordination ensured that all searches,
enquiries, and financial audits were executed simultaneously, preventing the flight of suspects or the concealment of illicit assets.
Brief Background: Unravelling the Transnational Cartel
The multi-state operation stems from sustained, intelligence-led backward and forward linkage investigations initiated by the NCB, Mizoram Police and Enforcement Directorate (ED) in the network cases identified for thorough 360-degree probe. Sustained probes unmasked a prolific transnational syndicate led by Myanmar-based kingpin Thangcintuang @ Chintuang @ Tluanga (wanted in over 10 NDPS cases across NCB, Champhai Police, and Mizoram Excise), who orchestrated the cross-border routing of Methamphetamine and Heroin across the Myanmar–Mizoram–Manipur–Assam–Tripura corridor into mainland India and Bangladesh. Prior phases of the investigation successfully neutralised key pillars of this cartel, including:
Thangcintuang @ Chintuang @ Tluanga (Kingpin): Arrested from Delhi following intensive inter-state surveillance, intelligence development, and sustained follow-up operations.
Vungkhanthawna (Key Facilitator): Close associate coordinating movement and delivery of Myanmar-origin consignments; arrested and subsequently detained under the stringent PITNDPS Act.
Lalrampari (Primary Hawala Operator): Arrested by NCB on 08.08.2024; investigations exposed nearly ₹100 Crore in illicit hawala transactions linked to the network, prompting joint action with the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and freezing of illegally acquired properties.
Abu Saleh @ Saifuddin (Assam Corridor Logistics Head): Arrested from Cachar, Assam on 20.11.2025; major Indian operative coordinating narcotics transportation across the Assam corridor and linked to multiple NDPS cases.
Detailed financial profiling and digital forensics from these breakthroughs revealed a wider web of facilitators, shell entities, and money mules, necessitating the massive, synchronized strike of Operation Trident.

title: National Urban Conclave 2026 concludes with actionable recommendations to strengthen urban governance, planning and service delivery towards Viksit Bharat 2047
subtitle:
“The intent of the Conclave is to deliberate on the future challenges of our cities”: Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs

Seven technical sessions outline key reforms for building inclusive, resilient and future-ready cities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 OCT 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
National Urban Conclave 2026 concluded in Bhubaneswar today  with actionable recommendations to strengthen urban governance, planning and service delivery towards Viksit Bharat 2047 .
Delivering the closing remarks, Shri Manohar Lal,
Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs reflected on India’s historical urban development trajectory and the Government of India’s continued efforts to strengthen urban infrastructure and services. Stating that “the intent of the Conclave is to deliberate on the future challenges of our cities”, he highlighted the progress achieved through national missions, including AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban and PM SVANidhi, in expanding water and sanitation services, improving waste management, strengthening urban mobility and promoting financial inclusion. He emphasised the importance of affordable housing near employment centres and public transport, circularity in construction practices, and the scientific remediation of legacy waste. Noting that over half of the country’s legacy waste has been remediated, he stressed the need to sustain these efforts and prevent the accumulation of new waste, ensuring that India's urban transformation remains inclusive, sustainable and future-ready.
Delivering the welcome address at the valedictory session of the National Urban Conclave 2026
, Shri Satendra Singh,
Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, reflected on the key outcomes of the seven technical sessions and emphasised the need to translate policy deliberations into practical, implementable urban solutions. He noted that “success should be measured by the quality of services, not merely by project completion”, an indication of the importance of strengthening institutional capacity, inter-agency coordination, municipal finances and accountability to improve service delivery. Highlighting the spirit of cooperative federalism, he reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to working with states, cities and partner institutions to take forward the Conclave’s recommendations, and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Delivering the special address,, Shri Rajiv Gauba,
Member, NITI Aayog emphasised the need for comprehensive reforms in urban governance, planning and municipal finance to manage India’s accelerating urban transition. Stating that, “we cannot run cities from our state capitals. We need to empower our smaller cities”, he called for greater devolution of powers and finances to urban local bodies, empowered city leadership and stronger municipal accountability. He stressed the importance of strengthening own-source revenues, reforming conventional land-use planning and promoting higher densities, mixed-use development and transit-oriented development to improve housing affordability and economic productivity. Highlighting initiatives such as the Urban Challenge Fund and City Economic Regions, he urged states to undertake structural reforms and called for linking funding under national urban missions to their implementation, enabling cities to realise their potential as engines of growth towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
The second and concluding day of the National Urban Conclave 2026 focused on translating policy deliberations into actionable recommendations for strengthening urban governance, planning, infrastructure and service delivery. Building on discussions across seven technical sessions, the Conclave brought together representatives from the Union and State Governments, urban local bodies, industry, academia and knowledge institutions to identify practical solutions for India's evolving urban challenges and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Takeaways from Technical Deliberations
The session on ‘Right to Walk’ addressed fragmented pedestrian spaces, poor accessibility, inadequate planning integration, unclear institutional responsibilities and funding gaps. The session recommended institutionalising the ‘Right to Walk’ in statutory plans, securing pedestrian right-of-way, strengthening ULB capacity and accountability, prioritising infrastructure quality and maintenance, adopting inclusive, community-led design, integrating pedestrian facilities into all street projects, and establishing dedicated financing mechanisms.
The session on ‘Water, Waste and Resource Efficiency’ recommended integrating water, wastewater and solid waste planning, shifting towards outcome-based service delivery, strengthening performance monitoring and lifecycle maintenance, promoting water reuse and circular resource recovery, developing markets for recovered resources, improving institutional accountability, and enabling sustainable financing through PPPs, municipal bonds and climate finance.
The session on ‘Affordable Housing – Demand and Supply Dynamics’ recommended reserving land for affordable housing, integrating housing with transit and employment centres, developing viable rental and transit housing models, introducing single-window approvals, leveraging FAR and TDR incentives for cross-subsidisation, strengthening government participation through housing boards and PPPs, and ensuring long-term affordability through quality construction and maintenance.
The session on ‘Integrated Urban Development and Infrastructure Delivery’ recommended integrating spatial and infrastructure planning through shared GIS-based databases, promoting corridor-based and transit-oriented development, aligning investments across sectors and agencies, implementing targeted, citizen-informed urban interventions, leveraging land-based financing mechanisms, strengthening municipal creditworthiness, and improving institutional coordination.
The session on ‘New Paradigms for Urban Service Delivery’ recommended shifting from asset creation to outcome-based service delivery, integrating municipal agencies around clearly defined responsibilities, strengthening digital monitoring and citizen feedback systems, institutionalising performance-based contracts, developing specialised municipal cadres, improving own-source revenue mobilisation, and establishing a national framework for accountable, citizen-centric urban services.
The session on ‘Model Building Bye-Laws’ recommended simplifying building regulations and approvals through integrated digital platforms, introducing risk-based scrutiny and self-certification, rationalising FAR, density and parking norms, enabling mixed-use and transit-oriented development, incorporating climate resilience and disaster safety standards, incentivising green construction, and improving regulatory transparency and ease of doing business.
The session on ‘Model Municipal Law’ recommended empowering Mayors with five-year tenures and clearly defined executive powers, strengthening devolution of municipal functions, improving coordination with parastatal agencies, enhancing fiscal autonomy and own-source revenues, ensuring adequate technical staffing, empowering Ward and Zonal Committees, and revising the Model Municipal Law, 2003, through state-level consultations and implementation frameworks.
Launches and Releases
Several initiatives and publications were launched during the second day of the Conclave:
Used Water Marketplace under AMRUT 2.0
A digital platform that connects urban local bodies (ULBs) with potential users and investors in the treated used-water ecosystem. ULBs can list the quantity and quality of treated water available for sale, enabling industries, institutions, and private entities to identify and access procurement opportunities.
UCF Portal
The portal is a key digital initiative that enables transparent, efficient and streamlined implementation of the Urban Challenge Fund. It serves as a common digital interface for states, Union Territories, ULBs and implementing agencies with project submission, tracking, appraisal and monitoring, and supporting decision-making.
Online Interactive Municipal Finance Data Hub
The multipurpose portal will connect the community of practitioners of municipal finance for two-way interactions via online discussion forums. It will also enable municipal reforms like enhancement of municipal revenue, and the availability of real-time digital data on municipal revenue and expenditure of ULBs.
Street Food Hubs under PM SVANidhi
An initiative to formally commence the development of the 18 selected Street Food Hubs under PM SVANidhi. The release of the first tranche of funds indicated the formal commencement of project implementation.
Swachhata Ke Superheroes
A book for children, created to instill the values of swachhata, waste segregation, and responsible waste management among young readers.
CPWD Nirman
A web and mobile application designed to enable digital monitoring of CPWD projects from initiation to completion. The platform will facilitate real-time progress tracking, milestone monitoring and inter-agency coordination, enhancing transparency, accountability and data-driven decision-making.
CPWDway
A digital capacity building platform offering short instructional videos on CPWD specifications, construction practices, project case studies, building services and architectural innovations. Integrated assessments will support continuous learning and practical skill development among government engineers and other engineering professionals.
Internship Scheme through the National Internship Portal
An initiative enabling undergraduate engineering and architecture students to access internship opportunities with CPWD through AICTE’s National Internship Portal. The scheme will provide practical exposure to government infrastructure projects, construction technologies, project management and quality assurance, strengthening industry–academia collaboration.
Technical Cooperation between JICA and CPHEEO
A Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and the Central Public Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation (CPHEEO) to strengthen technical cooperation in promoting the circular use of treated used water.
Conclusion of the Conclave
The recommendations emerging from the two-day National Urban Conclave 2026 will inform the next phase of urban reforms, with emphasis on stronger institutional capacity, integrated planning, sustainable financing and accountable service delivery.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi boosts morale of artisans by highlighting achievements of the Khadi and Village Industries sector in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme
subtitle:

date:

content:
Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India—expressed his heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. In the 139th episode of his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ programme, the Prime Minister highlighted the rising sales of Khadi and village industry products and urged citizens to prioritize products made by local artisans during the upcoming festive season. Shri Goel stated that this reassurance from the Prime Minister serves as a source of honour, motivation, and infused energy for the millions of artisans, weavers, crafts men and rural entrepreneurs across the country who are associated with the Khadi and Village Industries sector.
Shri Goel said that due to the continuous inspiration of Khadi and village industries by the Prime Minister, this sector has gone beyond its traditional identity and has become an important source of employment generation, women empowerment, strengthening of rural economy and building a self-reliant India. With the inspiration of the Prime Minister, Khadi today has become the cultural heritage of the country as well as the self-confidence of modern India. It has emerged as a symbol of the spirit of *Swadeshi* (indigenous) and economic empowerment.
Expressing his gratitude to the Prime Minister, KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel said, "The mention of Khadi and Village Industries in today’s episode—which coincides with the completion of 12 years of 'Mann Ki Baat'—is a moment of immense pride for us. It was from this very platform, on October 3, 2014, that the Prime Minister gave a call to purchase Khadi, thereby bestowing a new identity upon it. Since then, he has consistently encouraged purchase of Khadi and *Swadeshi* products. By highlighting that sales exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day on Gandhi Jayanti, he has significantly boosted the morale of millions of Khadi artisans, especially women. KVIC and all Khadi artisans across the country are deeply grateful to the Hon’ble Prime Minister. We pledge to further strengthen his vision of 'Vocal for Local' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-reliant India) through a focus on quality, innovation, and by engaging the younger generation." This episode was particularly significant as it marked the completion of 12 years of the 'Mann Ki Baat' program, which first began on October 3, 2014, on the occasion of Vijayadashami.
Shri Goel recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has, on several occasions through 'Mann Ki Baat', discussed the achievements of Khadi and appealed to the citizens of the country to purchase Khadi products. Following the appeal made in the very first episode on October 3, 2014—coinciding with Gandhi Jayanti—to buy at least one Khadi product, a record volume of sales was registered at the KVIC’s flagship outlet the very next day, on October 4, 2014. Subsequently, following similar appeals made on September 26, 2021 (in the 81st episode), September 25, 2022, and September 24, 2023, the Khadi Bhawan located at Connaught Place witnessed significant record sales of Rs. 1.34 crore on 2nd October in 2022, followed by over Rs 1.52 crore on October 2, 2023. In the 126th episode aired on September 28, 2025, the Prime Minister urged citizens to purchase at least one Khadi product on October 2 and take pride in its indigenous origin. Subsequently, in the 139th episode aired on October 25, 2026, he highlighted that sales of Khadi and Village Industries products had exceeded Rs 28 crore in a single day—on Gandhi Jayanti—and appealed to the public to buy local products during the festive season.
KVIC Chairman Shri Manoj Goel opined that, as a result of the visionary thinking and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Khadi and Village Industries sector has witnessed unprecedented growth. In the 2025-26 financial year, the turnover of this sector surpassed Rs 1.87 lakh crore, while providing employment to over 2.04 crore people. He assured that, in the near future, the sector would also reach its turnover target of Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

title: Sarbananda Sonowal to pitch India's Shipbuilding Opportunity to Korean Industry during Korea Visit
subtitle:

You can serve as living bridges between your networks in both countries: Sarbananda Sonowal to Indian shipbuilders in Korea

We are looking for partnership with Korea in shipbuilding, shipping, ports and maritime logistics: Sarbananda Sonowal
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                25 OCT 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal
began a four-day visit to South Korea from today, pitching India's maritime opportunity to Korean industry as the two countries work to expand shipbuilding cooperation and move India toward its goal of becoming one of the world's top five shipbuilding nations by 2047.
Sonowal opened the trip in Busan, which he called the hub of Korea's maritime industry, with an interaction with Indian professionals working in Korean shipbuilding.
India's Ambassador to South Korea, Gourangalal Das
, welcomed the gathering and introduced the community, which includes people from Samsung Heavy Industries, Hanwha Ocean, HD Hyundai, DNV and the Indian Register of Shipping.
"Your presence in Korea, at the heart of one of the world's most advanced shipbuilding ecosystems, is a matter of pride for India,"
Sonowal
said.
He urged them to see the framework adopted by the two countries in April, during South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit to India, as more than a government agreement. The framework, called VOYAGES, covers cooperation in shipbuilding, shipping and maritime logistics.
"I want you to see VOYAGES not merely as a government framework, but as a platform for your professional growth and for India's maritime future,"
Sonowal
said.
India aims to become a globally competitive centre for shipbuilding, ship repair, maritime manufacturing and logistics under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, Sonowal said. India's Cabinet approved a series of policy incentives for the sector in September 2025.
Sonowal said India will need many more shipbuilders, marine engineers, naval architects, designers, welders, project managers and technology specialists. He asked the professionals to bring their Korean experience home or to support Indian companies from Korea.
"You can serve as living bridges between your networks in both countries,"
Sonowal
said. He also encouraged them to mentor young Indian professionals and to take part in the India Ship Technology Centre and in the shipbuilding skills partnership between India and the Korea International Cooperation Agency.
Sonowal sought practical suggestions from the community on three issues: how to improve shipyard productivity and project execution, how to build a globally competitive skilled workforce, and how Indian and Korean industries can deepen cooperation in technology, manufacturing and innovation.
"We are looking for partnership with Korea in shipbuilding, shipping, ports and maritime logistics,"
Sonowal
said.
The schedule includes meetings with leaders of global shipbuilding industries, engaging with the maritime industry bodies and other maritime think tank & research institutions.
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal will take part in a ministerial roundtable in Busan for World Maritime Day, with ministerial representation from major maritime nations of the world, along with the secretary-general of the International Maritime Organisation (IMO), are expected.

ela

The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

title: “We can’t run cities from state capitals”: Shri Rajiv Gauba, Member, NITI Aayog at 2nd National Urban Conclave, calls for empowered city governments to Unlock India’s Growth Potential
date:
Posted On:
